description: Na₃Mg₂(MoO₄)₃ crystallizes in the monoclinic C2/c space group. There are three inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are four shorter (2.39 Å) and two longer (2.49 Å) Na-O bond lengths. In the second Na site, Na is bonded in a distorted hexagonal planar geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.43-2.64 Å. In the third Na site, Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.49-2.74 Å. Mg is bonded to six O atoms to form MgO₆ octahedra that share corners with six MoO₄ tetrahedra and  an edgeedge with one MgO₆ octahedra. There are a spread of Mg-O bond distances ranging from 2.05-2.34 Å. There are two inequivalent Mo sites. In the first Mo site, Mo is bonded to four O atoms to form MoO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four equivalent MgO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 59-61°. There are two shorter (1.87 Å) and two longer (1.88 Å) Mo-O bond lengths. In the second Mo site, Mo is bonded to four O atoms to form MoO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four equivalent MgO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 39-63°. There are a spread of Mo-O bond distances ranging from 1.75-1.83 Å. There are six inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Mg and one Mo atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a distorted trigonal planar geometry to one Na, one Mg, and one Mo atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to three Na and one Mo atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a trigonal planar geometry to one Na, one Mg, and one Mo atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na, one Mg, and one Mo atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded to two equivalent Na, one Mg, and one Mo atom to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing ONa₂MgMo trigonal pyramids.
